claims.value: other: bipolar neuron (two processes extending from the cell body)
claims.quote: Olfactory neurons are bipolar neurons (neurons with two processes extending from the cell body).

source.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: single dendrite, buried in the olfactory epithelium
claims.quote: Each neuron has a single dendrite buried in the olfactory epithelium

source.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: olfactory cilia: 5–20 hair-like, receptor-laden cilia extending from the dendrite
claims.quote: extending from this dendrite are 5 to 20 receptor-laden, hair-like cilia that trap odorant molecules

source.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: odorant receptor proteins on the cilia
claims.quote: The sensory receptors on the cilia are proteins, and it is the variations in their amino acid chains that make the receptors sensitive to different odorants.

source.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: G protein–coupled odorant receptors in the cell membrane of the dendrite
claims.quote: The odorant–protein complex binds to a receptor protein within the cell membrane of an olfactory dendrite. These receptors are G protein–coupled, and will produce a graded membrane potential in the olfactory neurons.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.quote: Olfactory neurons project from the olfactory epithelium to the olfactory bulb as thin, unmyelinated axons.

source.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: As a neuron that can detect chemical stimuli, it takes part in the sense of smell.
claims.quote: Any neuron that is capable of some detection of chemical stimulus involved in sensory perception of smell.

claims.value: Each neuron carries only one type of receptor on its cilia, so each neuron is specialized to detect specific odorants.
claims.quote: Each olfactory sensory neuron has only one type of receptor on its cilia, and the receptors are specialized to detect specific odorants, so the bipolar neurons themselves are specialized.

source.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: When its dendrite binds inhaled molecules, the neuron sends impulses directly to the olfactory bulb of the brain.
claims.quote: An olfactory receptor, which is a dendrite of a specialized neuron, responds when it binds certain molecules inhaled from the environment by sending impulses directly to the olfactory bulb of the brain.

source.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Olfactory neurons have a limited lifespan of about one to four months, and new ones are made regularly to take their place.
claims.quote: The sensory neurons of the olfactory epithelium have a limited lifespan of approximately one to four months, and new ones are made on a regular basis.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Because airborne toxic chemicals can harm the olfactory cells, the neurons are regularly replaced, and each new axon must find its connection in the olfactory bulb.
claims.quote: The nasal epithelium, including the olfactory cells, can be harmed by airborne toxic chemicals. Therefore, the olfactory neurons are regularly replaced within the nasal epithelium, after which the axons of the new neurons must find their appropriate connections in the olfactory bulb.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

tier1.text: Any neuron that is capable of some detection of chemical stimulus involved in sensory perception of smell.
